record.original_question: Construct a continuous theory for particles with positive and negative mass, or equivalently for billiards in pseudo-Euclidean metrics, and determine whether the resulting Euler-like equations for a fluid of negative density exhibit interesting phenomena.

evidence.quote: 3. Is there a fluid of negative density? Motivation:A mild reformulation of the question above is as follows:Study continuous versions for the interactions of particles of positive and negative mass. Explore the relation

corresponding theory and applications to gravitons are described in [18]. The problem is to construct a continuous version of this theory of particles of negative mass. Are there some interesting phenomena related to the corresponding Euler-like equations for the “fluid of negative density”?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of point particles in $\mathbb{R}^n$ in which each particle is assigned a mass $m_i \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}$ that may be positive or negative, with pairwise elastic interactions governed by conservation of momentum $\sum_i m_i v_i$ and kinetic energy $\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_i m_i \|v_i\|^2$. Equivalently, regard such a system as a billiard in a pseudo-Euclidean space whose metric is the indefinite quadratic form $Q(v)=\sum_i m_i\|v_i\|^2$ on the configuration space, with reflections at the walls $\{x_i=x_j\}$ governed by $Q$.

(a) Develop a continuum (hydrodynamic) limit of this discrete system: derive Euler-type equations governing a compressible fluid whose density field $\rho:\mathbb{R}^n\times \mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is allowed to take negative values, together with a velocity field $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ and pressure $p$, in such a way that the equations reduce, in the discrete (atomic) limit, to the elastic dynamics of mixed positive- and negative-mass particles described above.

(b) Analyze the resulting "negative-density Euler equations." In particular, determine whether they exhibit qualitatively new phenomena absent in the classical (positive-density) Euler equations — for example, instabilities at the zero-density interface $\{\rho=0\}$, runaway/self-acceleration solutions, formation of singularities, well-posedness or ill-posedness of the Cauchy problem, conserved quantities arising from the indefinite metric, or analogues of shocks and rarefaction waves with negative density.
artifact.status_search_result: No evidence was found of a worked-out continuum theory of fluids of negative density derived from pseudo-Euclidean billiards, nor of a systematic analysis of the corresponding Euler-like equations. The question appears to remain an open research direction.
